title: Taking counsel (ch. 3)
hook: the whole community is called, because God often reveals the better way to the youngest

segments.voice: Yesterday, the abbot: a father's name, holding the place of Christ, fitting his care to each person. Your line was each one differently. Whose needs did you ask about first? Today closes the week. Day one thousand one hundred ninety.

The grown-ups have been going around in circles all evening. Which car to sell, how to fit the move around school, who takes the dog. Then the youngest at the table, spooning up a bowl of cereal, says the obvious thing nobody had seen. The room goes quiet. Somebody laughs. And it's right, and everyone at the table knows it. Saint Benedict built that moment into the life of a monastery, on purpose. Today: taking counsel.
screen: `GOING AROUND IN CIRCLES.` → `THE YOUNGEST SAYS IT.` → `BENEDICT BUILDS IT IN.`

segments.voice: Chapter three of the Rule is short. Whenever something important has to be decided, the abbot is to call the whole community together and tell them what's at stake. Everyone. Not just the senior monks. Then he listens to their advice, thinks it over on his own, and does what he judges best. And here's the reason Benedict gives for calling everyone: because the Lord often shows what is better to the younger. The newest monk, the one with the least standing, may be the one who sees it. Benedict doesn't stop there. He tells the monks how to speak up: humbly, without stubbornly defending their own view. And he tells the abbot that he'll answer to God for what he decides, so he should decide fairly. The final call is still his. This isn't a vote. It's something quieter: a leader who has to hear the whole room before he chooses. The Bible has a story that fits. In the temple, the voice of God comes in the night, not to the old priest Eli, but to the boy Samuel. Eli tells him how to answer, and the boy says, in the Douay-Rheims: "Speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth." Look back at this week. Thomas's straw, and his last days at Fossanova. Many schools beside him. Then Benedict's first word, listen; a school for beginners; an abbot who fits himself to each person; and now an abbot who has to listen to the youngest. A whole week about who gets heard.
screen: `CALL THE WHOLE COMMUNITY.` · `GOD SHOWS THE YOUNGER WHAT'S BETTER.` · `SPEAK HUMBLY; THE ABBOT DECIDES.` · `A WEEK ABOUT WHO GETS HEARD.` · then, large: `SPEAK, LORD, FOR THY SERVANT HEARETH.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: ask a younger person's view. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind a decision you're carrying right now, big or small. Then bring to mind someone younger than you, or newer than you. A child, a niece, a new hire, a friend just starting out. Put the question the way you'd put it to them: one plain sentence, no background. Notice what drops away when it has to be that simple. If you pray, you can ask God to speak to you through whoever you least expect. The bell holds the time.
Taking counsel. In Benedict's Rule, the abbot calls the whole community before an important decision, because the Lord often shows what is better to the younger. Today's word.
Your line: the youngest may be right. Today, ask someone younger or newer what they think about one real decision, and listen to the end. That's the week. Day one thousand one hundred ninety.

howItsDone: In Benedictine monasteries the abbot or abbess consults the community in chapter before major decisions, as chapter 3 of the Rule describes, and then makes the decision.

pairs: God often shows the younger what's better
speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth

myth: in chapter 3, the monks vote and the majority wins
the abbot hears everyone, thinks it over, and decides. it isn't a vote.
Benedict says the Lord often shows what's better to the younger
that's his reason for calling the whole community.
only the senior monks are called for important matters
the Rule calls the whole community for important business.

fork.setup: you're the abbot, facing a big decision. who do you call to advise you?
options: only the oldest and wisest monks.
the whole community, down to the youngest.
no one: the abbot decides alone.
fork.reveal: Benedict says call everyone, because the Lord often shows what is better to the younger. then the abbot decides.

trapdoor: what you thought: a monastery is run strictly from the top down.
what it means: before big decisions the abbot must hear the whole community, down to the youngest, then decide.
what a scholar hears: Rule ch. 3, quia saepe iuniori Dominus revelat quod melius est; the monks advise humbly, and the abbot answers to God for the choice.

sources.quoted: Speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth.

notes: Chapter 3 is paraphrased (Gasquet 1909 wording unverified). Latin to confirm: 'Ideo autem omnes ad consilium vocari diximus, quia saepe iuniori Dominus revelat quod melius est.' Lesser matters go to the seniors only (not mentioned in the spoken script).
The Samuel story is offered by the script as a fitting example; the Rule does not cite it here.
Douay-Rheims wording to confirm: 1 Kings 3:10 ('Speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth').
